title: ab-testing: deterministic assignment core (bucketing + stickiness)
author: Jada Williams
description:
Motivation: We need a single, shared implementation for deterministic A/B assignment that can be called from routing (gateway/data-plane) and control-plane validation without duplicating hashing/bucketing logic. This PR introduces a small core library that: (1) deterministically assigns a request to a variant based on a configured traffic split, (2) supports stickiness via an explicit stable key + optional time window salt, and (3) exposes integration points/hooks expected by the policy engine and gateway.

Scope: Implements an `AssignmentEngine` with a stable hashing strategy and split bucketing, plus unit tests (incl. distribution sanity + determinism across retries). No persistence, no exposure logging, and no UI/config CRUD in this PR.

Design notes (aligned with ADR-0187 draft): - Inputs: assignment key is provided by caller as an opaque string; the library does not read request headers directly (keeps PII handling and availability concerns in the caller). - Determinism: uses xxhash64 over `experiment_id + assignment_key + stickiness_salt` and maps to [0, 9999] buckets for 0.01% granularity. - Stickiness: optional `stickiness_window_seconds`; when set, the library derives a time-window salt as `floor(request_unix_seconds / window)` so assignments remain stable within the window but can rotate between windows. - Retries/stream reconnect: caller should reuse the same assignment_key for the logical request; tests include idempotency with fixed inputs.

API sketch:
- `AssignmentEngine::assign(experiment_id, assignment_key, variants, stickiness)` -> `{ variant_id, bucket, hash }`
- `Split::validate()` ensures non-overlapping ranges and sum(traffic_bps)=10000.

Illustrative snippet:
`let out = engine.assign("exp_7H3...", key, vec![ ("control", 9000), ("treatment", 1000) ], Stickiness { window_seconds: Some(86400), ..Default::default() })?;`

Testing: - determinism tests across runs and platforms (golden vector test w/ fixed seed) - boundary tests (bucket 0/9999) - distribution sanity: 100k keys -> observed shares within tolerance (0.5%) - validation tests for malformed splits (sum != 10000, duplicates, empty variants)

Follow-ups: - Gateway PR will call this library to compute assignment and emit exposure events (ENG-2842) - Policy engine config model will embed split definitions and validation (ENG-2841) - Add allowlist enforcement for assignment_key derivation to avoid PII and high-cardinality spill (ADR-0188)

Risk: Low; library is not wired into production routing yet. Primary risk is future callers mis-constructing assignment keys; mitigated by docs + validation and by keeping key derivation outside this library.

Release notes: internal only; no user-visible behavior change until wired in.

review_conversation: Jordan Lee (review): Can we avoid taking raw request fields in here? I’d like the library to be 100% agnostic about headers/PII so we can enforce allowlists in the gateway/policy layer.
Jada Williams (author): Agree. Updated API to accept only `assignment_key: String` from the caller. Added README note that key derivation happens at call sites with allowlists.
Mina Haddad (review): Bucketing is 0..9999 which is good. Can you confirm we’re using integer bps and validating sum == 10000? Also please add tests for edge buckets and variant range boundaries.
Jada Williams (author): Added `Split::validate()` enforcing sum=10000 and non-overlap. Added boundary tests for bucket 0/9999 and off-by-one in range end.
Logan Wright (review): Distribution test is helpful, but please keep it stable in CI. The current tolerance looks tight and might flake depending on RNG/key generation.
Jada Williams (author): Updated to deterministic key generation with fixed seed; widened tolerance to 0.5% and reduced test runtime to keep CI under budget.
Marcus Lin (review): Please document that callers must not include email/usernames in assignment_key. Also consider adding a max length check to prevent accidental huge tags ending up in logs later.
Jada Williams (author): Added README guidance and a hard max length (256) on assignment_key with explicit error; callers can hash longer inputs upstream if needed.
Jordan Lee (approval): LGTM with the max length + caller-owned key derivation. This will make the policy precedence work easier in the next PR.
Mina Haddad (approval): Looks good. Please coordinate with Vikram/Amara when wiring into gateway so retries reuse the same key.
Logan Wright (approval): Approved. Thanks for the deterministic test vectors.
Marcus Lin (approval): Approved with the README + length guard.
